newsitem.title: USA: Ohio gov signs longer period for library tax notes.
newsitem.headline: Ohio gov signs longer period for library tax notes.

text.p: Ohio Gov. George Voinovich on Wednesday signed legislation allowing library districts to issue tax anticipation notes backed by voter-approved levies for up to 10 years, double the former period.

The five year limit for issuance of notes had been in place a number of years and originated when levies had to face voter approval every five years, said Mike Mooney, a legislative aide to the bill's sponsor, Ohio Sen. Roy Ray, R-Akron.
Some voter approved levies now run 20 years and the bill had no opposition, Mooney said.
The bill becomes effective 90 days following Voinovich's signing and filing with the Ohio secretary of state's office.
